moved.sentence: Expected vs exceptional: model recoverable outcomes (not-found, validation-failed, conflict) as returned values; let exceptions signal bugs and unrecoverable states.

judged.note: should-model-recoverable-outcomes-as-values keeps recoverable outcomes with examples as returned values; should-reserve-exceptions-for-unrecoverable keeps exceptions for bugs and unrecoverable states, both SHOULD.

moved.sentence: Put the failure in the signature: a function that can fail should say so in its return type, not through an undeclared throw a caller can't see.

judged.note: should-put-the-failure-in-the-signature keeps the 'should' at SHOULD: a failing function says so in its return type, not an undeclared throw.

moved.sentence: Choose a boundary policy deliberately and keep it consistent per layer: Rust `Result`, Go explicit error returns, Kotlin sealed `Result`, Swift `Result`/`throws`, TypeScript Result-style libraries.

judged.note: should-keep-boundary-policy-consistent-per-layer keeps choosing the policy deliberately, per-layer consistency, and all five language examples.

moved.sentence: Never swallow: log-and-continue, a silent `null`, or a default that masks failure is the documented failure mode — propagate or handle explicitly.

judged.note: must-not-swallow-failures keeps 'never swallow' as MUST NOT, all three failure modes, and propagate-or-handle-explicitly as MUST.
